decisive_items: Heart deviated the tracheobronchial tree to the right, compressed left bronchus, and occupied almost the entire left hemithorax
Decreased size of the cardiac allograft, relieved compression of left bronchus, improved expansion of left lung
Further size remodeling of the cardiac allograft and only mild residual compression of the left bronchus
response.rationale: Serial post-operative CTs show a large cardiac allograft compressing the left bronchus and then remodeling over time, directly indicating a post-heart-transplantation complication rather than LVAD, cardiomyopathy, or a purely respiratory/generic diagnosis.

rejected.why: Explains pre-transplant embolic strokes/LVAD but not the post-transplant cardiac allograft and bronchial compression.
Focused on LVAD, while the post-operative CT explicitly concerns the cardiac allograft after transplantation.
Embolic stroke was the presentation but is not the diagnosis reflected by serial post-transplant CT findings.
Too nonspecific and unsupported compared with the precise allograft-related complication.
Cardiomyopathy is contradicted by LVAD and transplant context; echocardiographic measures are nonspecific monitoring.
Echocardiographic parameters are monitoring tools, not a diagnosis and do not explain CT findings.
No evidence for pulmonary embolism in the imaging findings.
Growth measurements are demographic data, not the diagnosis.
No support for hypoplasia; the allograft is post-transplant, not a native hypoplastic heart.
Overly broad cardiac disease label; the specific transplant complication is better supported.
Bronchial compression is secondary to the oversized allograft, not a primary respiratory disease.
